A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Reference Grounded Skill Discovery by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original humanoid simulation results, including imitation error and FID in Table 1, downstream performance in Figure 5, and encoder-alignment measurements in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results, including imitation, skill-discovery, downstream-control, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F retain the same contrastive pretraining, DIAYN-derived reward, parallel imitation/discovery, reference-state initialization, and encoder regularization. The architecture and algorithm steps are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same 20 ACCAD reference motions and SMPL humanoid, covering walking, running, sidestepping, backward motion, and punching. The freestyle, sidestepping, and backward goal-reaching scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 4 retain DIAYN, METRA, ASE, CALM, and Meta-Motivo; Figure 5 retains ASE, CALM, and Meta-Motivo. The newly cited Periodic Skill Discovery is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 retain the 500-trajectory imitation evaluations, latent-selection procedure, diversity sampling settings, metrics, and hierarchical goal-reaching protocol. Appendix G's baseline adjustments and hyperparameters are identical.

E4.justification: The diversity sensitivity experiment in Appendix A, encoder-alignment analysis in Appendix E, and METRA variant investigation in Section 6 and Appendix H are retained unchanged. Figure 6's revised caption introduces no additional analysis.

E5.justification: The three-random-seed statement in Section 5.3, shaded curves in Figure 5, and mean-plus/minus alignment statistic in Appendix E are unchanged. No statistical tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures are added.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical scores, Figures 4–6's trajectories, curves and FID annotations, and Appendix E's alignment value of 0.99998 ± 8.91 × 10^-6 are identical. The qualitative skill examples and METRA failure findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, InfoNCE derivation, within-motion alignment proof, and reward optimality and local quasi-concavity arguments retain the same assumptions and reasoning. Section 6's added citation does not revise its mathematical argument.

C1.justification: Figure 1's introductory caption changes from stating that RGSD discovers structured high-DoF skills to a qualified claim that this is the first work to do so by grounding skills in reference motions. The principal method, performance, and theoretical contribution claims otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The fidelity–naturalness trade-off, latent-neighborhood generalization explanation, METRA failure mechanisms, and discussion of overlapping states and future compositional or cross-embodiment skills are unchanged. Figure 6's expanded caption repeats the diversity interpretation already present in v2's Section 5.2.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-video address on page 1 and removes v2's promise to release the full codebase upon acceptance. Implementation details, motion filenames, and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish actual code-release status.

R1.justification: Section 6 newly cites Park et al.'s Periodic Skill Discovery as concurrent work consistent with the repetitive-motion limitation. Figure 1 also adds explicit first-work positioning. The remaining research positioning is substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the abstract, revises the opening introduction example, adds acknowledgments and an affiliation address, and replaces Preprint headers with ICLR 2026 publication headers. The main section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 6 receive revised captions, and the first page and endmatter reflow, including moving the reproducibility heading to page 11. Figure panels, axes, legends, and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The clearer Figure 6 caption, video address, and concurrent-work attribution provide modest presentation and context improvements. However, the scientific evidence, proofs, and implementation instructions remain identical, while the code-release commitment disappears without a release-status statement. These limited edits leave the paper's overall evidential strength and practical reproducibility essentially unchanged.
